submission_brief.summary: Northstar Analytics Inc. (Tech E&O, SaaS / B2B Software) is ready to quote with Apex (carrier-apex). The email and application agree on class, revenue ($4.2M), limit ($2M), effective date (2026-12-01) and a clean loss history. Both documents are v1 and nothing is superseded. All Apex required fields are present, and the risk is within Apex's appetite: the class is eligible and not prohibited, revenue is under $25M, the limit is under $5M, and incurred losses are $0. Ironclad is out of appetite for SaaS. Caveats: (1) the email says a loss history is attached, but no separate loss run is in the submission, so the loss history comes only from the application and is unverified. Consider requesting the carrier loss run as a subject-to condition. (2) The application text shows no signature or date. Neither caveat changes the disposition.

submission_brief.summary: Human review required for Summit Exterior Solutions LLC. The broker email says IT & Management Consulting, but the signed ACORD application says Commercial Roofing Contractor (85% of revenue from roofing). Revenue ($5.1M), limit ($2M), and effective date (2026-12-01) match across both documents. Both carriers (Apex and Ironclad) prohibit Roofing Contractor, so the risk is outside all available appetite and no carrier match is possible. Apex also requires contradictions to be routed to human underwriting review. The location schedule is missing and no loss run is attached to verify the reported 0 claims. Do not quote under the IT consulting class; ask the broker to explain the discrepancy and, if the insured is a roofer, seek a market outside these carriers.

submission_brief.summary: Routed to human_review. The broker email classifies the risk as IT & Management Consulting, but the signed ACORD application (treated as controlling) shows a Commercial Roofing Contractor with 85% of revenue from roofing work. Roofing Contractor is prohibited by both Apex and Ironclad, so the signed class is outside all available carrier appetite, and no carrier match is made. Revenue ($5,100,000), limit ($2,000,000), effective date (2026-12-01) and the self-reported clean loss history agree across both documents. No loss run is attached, and there is no location schedule or coverage line. Missing documents would not change the outcome. An underwriter or compliance reviewer should assess possible misrepresentation. Broker questions: confirm true operations and class with a revenue split; provide currently valued 3-year loss runs; state the coverage line; explain the 'Tech Consulting' name in the email title; for Ironclad only, provide a location schedule and, if workers' comp applies, a payroll breakdown by class code.
